# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by `python manage.py export_tool_reference`. Do not edit by hand. -->

60 tools are registered. The planner sees only the built-in tools plus tools whose integration the user has connected.

- **Confirm**: the chat agent asks for approval before running the tool. Saved and scheduled workflow runs do not ask yet (see the roadmap).
- `*` marks a required parameter. Credentials and the user ID are injected by the orchestrator and never appear in plans.
- None of these tools has been verified against a live provider yet.

## Built-in tools

No account connection needed. Some need an operator API key (see configuration.md).

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contacts.create` |  | `first_name`* (string), `last_name` (string), `alias` (string), `email` (string) | Create a new contact for the user. |
| `contacts.delete` | yes | `contact_id`* (integer) | Permanently delete a contact from the user's address book. |
| `contacts.search` |  | `query`* (string), `limit` (integer) | Search the user's contacts by name, alias, or email address. |
| `contacts.update` |  | `contact_id`* (integer), `first_name` (string), `last_name` (string), `alias` (string), `email` (string) | Update an existing contact. Only provided (non-empty) fields are changed. |
| `memory.delete` |  | `key`* (string) | Delete a previously saved memory by key. Use when the user asks you to forget something or when a stored fact is no longer accurate. |
| `memory.save` |  | `key`* (string), `value`* (string) | Save or update a persistent memory about the user. Use this to remember facts, preferences, or context that should persist across conversations. Examples: user's name, location, preferences, ongoing goals, or anything the user asks you to remember. |
| `processing_llm` |  | `task`* (string), `inputs` (object) | Call the LLM to synthesize, summarize, or transform data from prior steps into a natural-language string. Can appear at any point in the plan — use it to compose content (e.g. an email body) before passing to the next step, or as the final step to produce a human-readable answer. |
| `weather.get_current_weather` |  | `city`* (string) | Fetch current weather conditions for a city. |
| `weather.get_weather_by_coordinates` |  | `lat`* (number), `lon`* (number) | Fetch current weather conditions by geographic coordinates. |
| `weather.get_weather_forecast` |  | `city`* (string), `days` (integer) | Fetch a daily weather forecast for up to 5 days for a city. |
| `web.search` |  | `query`* (string), `max_results` (integer), `include_answer` (boolean) | Search the web for current information. Returns a ranked list of results with titles, URLs, and content snippets. Use for current events, factual lookups, research, or any question that may require up-to-date information not in the model's training data. |
| `workflow.list` |  | — | List all of the user's saved workflows by name and ID. |
| `workflow.save` |  | `name`* (string), `plan`* (object), `description` (string), `input_schema` (array) | Save a plan as a reusable named workflow. Use this when the user asks to save, create, or name a workflow. The 'plan' param is the complete inner workflow plan (its own steps/final_output_var/summary). In the inner plan, replace any params the user would want to vary between runs with '$input.<name>' references, and list those in 'input_schema' with human-readable labels. |

## Google / Gmail (`gmail`)

OAuth scopes requested: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gmail.add_label` |  | `msg_id`* (string), `label_name`* (string) | Apply a Gmail label to a message by label name. |
| `gmail.create_draft` |  | `to`* (array), `subject`* (string), `body`* (string), `cc` (array), `bcc` (array) | Save a composed email as a Gmail draft without sending it. |
| `gmail.get_attachment` |  | `msg_id`* (string), `attachment_id`* (string) | Fetch the content of an email attachment. Use this when the user asks to read, summarise, or act on an attachment. The msg_id and attachment_id come from a prior gmail fetch step. |
| `gmail.get_drafts` |  | `max_results` (integer) | Fetch email drafts from Gmail. |
| `gmail.get_label_emails` |  | `label`* (string), `max_results` (integer), `hours_ago` (integer) | Fetch emails for a specific Gmail label. |
| `gmail.get_next_page` |  | `max_results` (integer) | Fetch the next page of emails from the most recent Gmail query in this session. Use this when the user asks to see more emails after a prior fetch - e.g. 'show me more', 'next page', 'load more emails'. |
| `gmail.get_sent_emails` |  | `max_results` (integer), `hours_ago` (integer) | Fetch sent emails from Gmail. |
| `gmail.get_starred_emails` |  | `max_results` (integer), `hours_ago` (integer) | Fetch starred emails from Gmail. |
| `gmail.get_unread_emails` |  | `max_results` (integer), `hours_ago` (integer) | Fetch unread emails from the Gmail inbox. |
| `gmail.mark_read` |  | `msg_id`* (string) | Mark a Gmail message as read (removes the UNREAD label). |
| `gmail.mark_unread` |  | `msg_id`* (string) | Mark a Gmail message as unread (adds the UNREAD label). |
| `gmail.remove_label` |  | `msg_id`* (string), `label_name`* (string) | Remove a Gmail label from a message by label name. |
| `gmail.reply_email` | yes | `msg_id`* (string), `body`* (string), `cc` (array), `bcc` (array) | Reply to an existing Gmail message in-thread. Automatically sets In-Reply-To and References headers and places the reply in the correct Gmail thread. Use this instead of gmail.send_email when replying. The msg_id comes from a prior gmail fetch or search step. |
| `gmail.search_emails` |  | `keywords`* (array), `max_results` (integer), `hours_ago` (integer) | Search Gmail for emails whose subject or body matches the given keywords, optionally filtered by recency. |
| `gmail.send_draft` | yes | `draft_id`* (string) | Send an existing Gmail draft by its draft ID. |
| `gmail.send_email` | yes | `to`* (array), `subject`* (string), `body`* (string), `cc` (array), `bcc` (array), `reply_to` (string) | Send a new plain-text email via Gmail. |
| `gmail.trash_email` | yes | `msg_id`* (string) | Move a Gmail message to Trash by its message ID. |

## Google Calendar (`google_calendar`)

OAuth scopes requested: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events`

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calendar.create_event` | yes | `summary`* (string), `start`* (string), `end`* (string), `description` (string), `location` (string), `attendees` (array), `calendar_id` (string), `recurrence` (array) | Create a new event on the user's Google Calendar. |
| `calendar.delete_event` | yes | `event_id`* (string), `calendar_id` (string) | Permanently delete an event from the user's Google Calendar. |
| `calendar.get_free_busy` |  | `time_min`* (string), `time_max`* (string), `calendar_ids` (array) | Check when the user is free or busy over a time range. Returns a list of busy slots per calendar. Use this to answer questions like 'when am I free next week?' or 'do I have any conflicts on Thursday?' |
| `calendar.list_calendars` |  | — | List all Google Calendars the user has access to. Returns each calendar's ID, name, and access role. Use this to discover non-primary calendar IDs before listing or creating events. |
| `calendar.list_events` |  | `max_results` (integer), `time_min` (string), `time_max` (string), `query` (string), `calendar_id` (string) | List the user's Google Calendar events. Returns event titles, times, locations, and attendees. |
| `calendar.update_event` | yes | `event_id`* (string), `summary` (string), `start` (string), `end` (string), `description` (string), `location` (string), `calendar_id` (string) | Update an existing event on the user's Google Calendar. Only supplied fields are changed. |

## Google Contacts (`google_contacts`)

OAuth scopes requested: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/contacts.readonly`

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `google_contacts.list` |  | `max_results` (integer) | List the user's Google contacts including names, email addresses, and phone numbers. |
| `google_contacts.search` |  | `query`* (string), `max_results` (integer) | Search the user's Google contacts by name or email address. |
| `google_contacts.sync` |  | — | Import all Google contacts into the Aiva contact database. Contacts are matched by email address - existing records are updated, new ones are created. Contacts without an email address are skipped. |

## Google Drive (`google_drive`)

OAuth scopes requested: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly`

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drive.get_file_metadata` |  | `file_id`* (string) | Return detailed metadata for a single Google Drive file or folder. |
| `drive.list_files` |  | `max_results` (integer), `folder_id` (string) | List the user's recent Google Drive files and folders. Returns metadata only, not file contents. |
| `drive.read_file` |  | `file_id`* (string) | Read the text content of a Google Drive file. Supports Google Docs (exported as plain text), Google Sheets (exported as CSV), Google Slides (exported as plain text), and plain-text files. Binary files (images, PDFs, videos) cannot be read and will return an error. Content is truncated at 50,000 characters for large files. |
| `drive.search_files` |  | `query`* (string), `max_results` (integer), `folder_id` (string) | Search the user's Google Drive files by name. Returns metadata only, not file contents. |

## Notion (`notion`)

OAuth scopes requested: none (set on the integration)

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notion.append_blocks` | yes | `page_id`* (string), `blocks`* (array) | Append block children (verbatim Notion block objects) to a Notion page or block. |
| `notion.create_page` | yes | `parent_id`* (string), `title`* (string), `content` (string), `is_database` (boolean) | Create a Notion page under a parent page, or as a row in a database when is_database is true. Optional content is split on newlines into paragraph blocks. |
| `notion.get_page` |  | `page_id`* (string) | Fetch a Notion page's properties together with its top-level child blocks (the page body). |
| `notion.list_databases` |  | `page_size` (integer) | List Notion databases the integration can access. |
| `notion.query_database` |  | `database_id`* (string), `filter` (object), `sorts` (array) | Query rows (pages) in a Notion database with optional Notion filter and sort objects. |
| `notion.search` |  | `query`* (string), `filter_type` (string) | Search Notion pages and databases by title. Optionally filter to only 'page' or 'database' objects. |
| `notion.update_page` | yes | `page_id`* (string), `title` (string), `properties` (object) | Update a Notion page's properties. Only supplied fields are changed. |

## Outlook Mail (`outlook`)

OAuth scopes requested: `https://graph.microsoft.com/Mail.Read`, `https://graph.microsoft.com/Mail.Send`, `offline_access`

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outlook.get_emails` |  | `max_results` (integer), `folder` (string) | Fetch recent emails from an Outlook folder (inbox, sentitems, drafts, deleteditems). |
| `outlook.get_unread_emails` |  | `max_results` (integer) | Fetch unread emails from Outlook / Microsoft 365. |
| `outlook.reply_email` | yes | `message_id`* (string), `body`* (string) | Reply to an Outlook message in-thread. The reply is automatically addressed to the sender. The message_id comes from a prior outlook.get_* or search step. |
| `outlook.search_emails` |  | `query`* (string), `max_results` (integer) | Search Outlook emails by keyword or KQL query. Supports 'subject:budget', 'from:john@example.com', or plain keywords. |
| `outlook.send_email` | yes | `to`* (array), `subject`* (string), `body`* (string), `cc` (array), `bcc` (array) | Send a plain-text email via Outlook. |

## Outlook Calendar (`outlook_calendar`)

OAuth scopes requested: `https://graph.microsoft.com/Calendars.ReadWrite`, `offline_access`

| Tool | Confirm | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outlook_calendar.create_event` | yes | `subject`* (string), `start`* (string), `end`* (string), `description` (string), `location` (string), `attendees` (array), `timezone` (string), `is_online_meeting` (boolean) | Create a new event on the user's Outlook Calendar. |
| `outlook_calendar.delete_event` | yes | `event_id`* (string) | Permanently delete an Outlook Calendar event. |
| `outlook_calendar.get_free_busy` |  | `time_min`* (string), `time_max`* (string) | Check when the user is free or busy by listing all calendar events in a time range. Use this to answer 'when am I free next week?' or 'do I have conflicts on Thursday?' |
| `outlook_calendar.list_events` |  | `max_results` (integer), `time_min` (string), `time_max` (string) | List Outlook Calendar events. Provide time_min and time_max to restrict to a date range; omit for upcoming events. |
| `outlook_calendar.update_event` | yes | `event_id`* (string), `subject` (string), `start` (string), `end` (string), `description` (string), `location` (string), `timezone` (string) | Update an existing Outlook Calendar event. Only supplied fields are changed. |
